problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y=\frac{1}{2}{(\frac{1}{4})}^{x}-3?$
worked_solution:
We start with plotting the graph of $y={(\frac{1}{4})}^{x}:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931416/assets/e648e3a5f0c844d6596d4848629c3e6749647228116bcc5da6fce250895141d5.png)

Next, we plot the graph of $y=\frac{1}{2}{(\frac{1}{4})}^{x}.$ To do this, we scale the graph above by a factor of $\frac{1}{2}.$ The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,1)$ to $(0,\frac{1}{2})$ but the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931416/assets/378016bbd17371e3dfee1e80934e76b1357139d405cb320ac5befa252da82b28.png)

Finally, we plot the graph of $y=\frac{1}{2}{(\frac{1}{4})}^{x}-3.$ To do this, we shift the above graph $3$ units down. The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,\frac{1}{2})$ to $(0,-\frac{5}{2})$ and the horizontal asymptote moves from $y=0$ to $y=-3.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931416/assets/e545a84145ac0a139ee5ecdf9692c20837d211f9a70fd79ad33dd13f60c856f7.png)
